newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy prosecution seeks 23 yrs for US boy murder.
newsitem.headline: Italy prosecution seeks 23 yrs for US boy murder.

text.p: An Italian prosecutor in the southern town of Catanzaro on Monday sought jail terms of 23 years for each of the two men accused of killing a seven-year-old American boy in a motorway hold-up.

Magistrate Maurizio Salustro said he had not sought life imprisonment for Francesco Mesiano, 23 and Michele Iannello, 28, in the September 1994 murder of Nicholas Green because of extenuating circumstances.

Mesiano, who was released from jail last month on health grounds, does not have a serious criminal record and although Iannello has admitted to four murders, he has turned state's evidence and is living under a witness protection scheme.
Both men say they are innocent of the Green murder.

Nicholas was on holiday in southern Italy with his family, from Bodega Bay, California, when their hired car was chased and shot at on a motorway in an attempted hold-up. He was hit in the head as he slept on the back seat next to his sister.
The family's apparent lack of rancour and their decision to donate the boy's organs, which saved the lives of six young Italians, stunned Italy and earned the Greens deep respect.
Nicholas's father, Reginald, was in court but declined to comment until sentencing. The trial was expected to conclude on Tuesday.
